chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: “Cursed, cursed is the one who delays the Maghrib prayer seeking its supposed extra merit.”
And it was said to him: The people of Iraq delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars interlace, so he said: “This is from the practice of the enemy of Allah, Abī al-Khaṭṭāb.”

key_terms.أَبِي الْخَطَّابِ: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb, the individual blamed for this practice
key_terms.أَخَّرَ: delayed beyond its proper time or immediate performance
key_terms.تَشْتَبِكَ النُّجُومُ: the stars become visibly interwoven or densely apparent in the sky
key_terms.طَلَبًا لِفَضْلِهَا: seeking an assumed extra merit for delaying it

ai.seo_question: Is it recommended to delay the Maghrib prayer until the stars appear?
ai.summary: This hadith condemns delaying salat al-Maghrib in pursuit of an imagined added virtue. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rejects the practice of postponing it until the stars become prominent and attributes that practice to Abū al-Khaṭṭāb.
